strengths.title: How they set up as a pair
strengths.body: The two opponents stood side by side for 84% and 81% of play and front-and-back for 8% and 10%; they were within 1.5 m of each other across the court for 48% and 56% of the time. They defend as a tight pair around the middle.
strengths.sure: Pair numbers from positions only: no shot data. Solid when they were near the camera, rougher when far.

weaknesses.title: Wide sidelines
weaknesses.body: Because they bunch (within 1.5 m across for more than half the time), the outer 2 m or more on each side of their half is often unguarded.
weaknesses.sure: Approximate; width is the more reliable direction of the tracking.

weaknesses.title: The front court was left empty in game 2
weaknesses.body: In game 2 the opponents spent only 3% to 6% of play in the front court (the first 2.2 m from the net) and stood on average 3.8 m from the net (your pair 3.8 m). If that is how they defend, short net shots and drops are the space they leave.
weaknesses.sure: Position only: it does not show whether net shots won points against them.

plan.title: Test the space they leave
plan.body: Mix soft shots to the net and wide cross-court shots into your usual exchanges, and watch the longest plays listed at the end to see how they respond.
plan.try: Pick two plays per game to rewatch and note where each opponent was when you hit the shuttle.
plan.sure: This is a hypothesis from positions only. The score is not in the video, so it cannot say which tactic won points.
